setup.title: Setup wizard
setup.sub: Five steps and {brand} can start working for you
setup.banner.text: Take two minutes to set up {brand} (model key, phone, safety defaults)
setup.loadFailed: Could not read how far the setup got: {reason}
setup.mark.skipped: Left for later — you can come back any time
setup.rail.label: The steps of the wizard
setup.steps.language.title: Language, how to call you, assistant name
setup.steps.language.sub: Which language the interface uses, what it calls you, and the assistant's name
setup.steps.language.assistantNameNote: The name and voice are changed in Roles & voices; the whole interface follows
setup.steps.model.title: Model key
setup.steps.model.sub: Without the key it cannot answer; once this is set up you can talk to it
setup.steps.model.where: The key is saved into the secret area of the data directory (the supervisor hands it to the assistant at startup). Paste it below and save — no restart needed; you can change it later under Settings · Models.
setup.steps.components.title: Components (the vector model for memory)
setup.steps.components.sub: Memory finds materials by meaning, which needs the vector model (about 570 MB to download); it can also be fetched later
setup.steps.components.unknown: The component list does not have it
setup.steps.phone.title: Pair your phone
setup.steps.phone.sub: Open the outside address on a phone or tablet: the page shows a six-digit code and a pairing request appears in the inbox on this computer. Check that they match, then approve
setup.steps.phone.notReady: No device paired yet (no rush, use this computer first)
setup.steps.phone.how: How to expose the outside address is on the last page of this wizard, Access from outside, or the Outside access section of the user guide.
setup.steps.safety.title: Safety defaults
setup.steps.safety.sub: A fresh install is tight: risky things ask you first and tasks stop when they go over budget. Turn either off whenever it gets in your way.
setup.done.title: Setup is done — go use it
setup.done.sub: Anything you want to change later is in More · Settings.
setup.done.external: Want to use it from outside? See Access from outside
setup.external.title: Access from outside
setup.external.intro: By default {brand} is only used on this computer. To use it on a phone or tablet there are three ways, and the first one is recommended.
setup.external.port: All three only expose the outside port 8811: every request there needs a device credential, and a new device must be approved by you on this computer. Never expose the local port 8810.
setup.external.tailscale.title: Way one: Tailscale (recommended)
setup.external.tailscale.sub: Install Tailscale on the computer and the phone, sign in with the same account, and use tailscale serve to offer 8811 over HTTPS to your tailnet. The address is:
setup.external.headscale.title: Way two: self-hosted Headscale (advanced)
setup.external.headscale.sub: Run Headscale on a VPS and sign both the computer and the phone in to it, then hang 8811 on the supervisor's tailnet entry point. The address is:
setup.external.vps.title: Way three: VPS + ssh reverse tunnel + nginx (public)
setup.external.vps.sub: One VPS and a domain certificate; nginx terminates HTTPS and forwards through an ssh reverse tunnel to port 8811 on this computer. The address is:
setup.external.guide: This version only spells out the three ways, it does not configure them; the detailed steps are in the Outside access section of the user guide.
